scope: Public evidence extracts for #95–#101 and #104–#105; partial coverage, no historical or full product validation

patterns.name: Question filtering and saved filters
patterns.definition: Combine exam attributes, keyword and exclusions; make the applied criteria visible and removable.
patterns.guardrail: Do not confuse employer, examining board, position, exam year and discipline. Do not assume unseen filter states.
patterns.tests: Given a saved filter, restore the same criteria; verify zero results and clearing a single criterion.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: Question notebook and saved sets
patterns.definition: Distinguish a selected question set from a live filter and a scored attempt.
patterns.guardrail: The documentation describes creating notebooks; it is not proof of how all mobile or offline states work.
patterns.tests: Check set membership, duplicates, empty set, and changes to source questions.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: Retrieval and distributed practice
patterns.definition: Plan opportunities to recall information and distribute study across time, rather than only reread material.
patterns.guardrail: Evidence for learning techniques is not validation of a particular app or scheduling algorithm; retention and transfer differ.
patterns.tests: Compare delayed recall using equivalent items and record exposure, study time and attrition.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: Assessment item and test interoperability
patterns.definition: Separate assessment item, test, response and result; use QTI for portable structured assessments where required.
patterns.guardrail: Interoperability does not imply validity or calibrated difficulty. Do not apply IRT without calibration data.
patterns.tests: Round-trip an original fictional item and check response identifiers, scoring and result versioning.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: Typed knowledge objects and relations
patterns.definition: Model reusable connected objects rather than forcing every record into a file hierarchy.
patterns.guardrail: Documentation establishes the object-oriented concept, not all interaction states or historical app decisions.
patterns.tests: Check stable identity, reference integrity, missing target and reversible type changes.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: Typed nodes and fields
patterns.definition: Use explicit type and field definitions for structured nodes; views can present the same data in different contexts.
patterns.guardrail: Do not assume inheritance, sync or deletion semantics without feature-specific evidence.
patterns.tests: Check required/optional fields, type changes and stale references in original examples.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: Annotation anchor resilience
patterns.definition: Separate annotation body, target and selector. Text quotes with context can help reanchor; positions are vulnerable to content edits.
patterns.guardrail: Never silently reattach an ambiguous selection; avoid copying restricted text into exported annotations.
patterns.tests: Test version change, repeated quotes, no match, changed offsets and explicit unresolved state.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation
patterns.demo_scope: Original ASCII text quote or fictional discrete selection; not full product conformance.

patterns.name: Accessible component behavior contract
patterns.definition: Define semantics, input behavior, keyboard, focus and states separately from visual tokens.
patterns.guardrail: Library accessibility claims do not establish product-level conformance; verify actual composition.
patterns.tests: Exercise keyboard, pointer and touch; test disabled, busy and invalid states and accessible names.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: ARIA widget interaction patterns
patterns.definition: Select the matching widget semantics and keyboard interaction contract; prefer native elements where appropriate.
patterns.guardrail: APG is implementation guidance, not a substitute for WCAG conformance testing.
patterns.tests: Validate accessible role/name/state, focus sequence and restoration, and screen-reader operation.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: Data visualization palette semantics
patterns.definition: Choose categorical colors for unordered categories, sequential for magnitude, and diverging for a meaningful center.
patterns.guardrail: Color must not be the only cue; distinguish missing values from zero and category from status.
patterns.tests: Check legend/labels, contrast, textual alternative and meaningful ordering with original sample data.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: Saved filters and exam attempts
patterns.definition: Save and reopen search criteria independently of the scored attempt. The help article places save and reopen controls below filtering.
patterns.guardrail: Do not assume that a saved filter freezes the set of items; distinguish query definition, notebook membership and attempt snapshot.
patterns.tests: Change the source set and compare saved query results against immutable attempt membership.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: FSRS review scheduling
patterns.definition: Deck settings include scheduling, desired retention, daily review limits and FSRS parameters. Higher retention targets trade review workload against expected forgetting.
patterns.guardrail: A target retention is an algorithmic objective, not a guaranteed outcome. Preserve review history and model version.
patterns.tests: Use fictional review histories, test schedule reproducibility and compare calibration on independent delayed recall.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: Learning activity event interoperability
patterns.definition: Use shared event vocabularies and profiles to capture learning activity across providers.
patterns.guardrail: Activity is not the same as measured learning outcome; avoid causal claims from clicks and time spent.
patterns.tests: Validate event schema, duplicate delivery, timestamps and distinction between event and scored outcome.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: Object query versus collection
patterns.definition: Queries can filter by object type, tags and linked objects. Model dynamic query results separately from explicit collections.
patterns.guardrail: Do not infer every product state from the documentation; preserve object identity and permissions.
patterns.tests: Compare a saved query before and after tag changes, and test inaccessible and deleted references.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: Combobox popup focus
patterns.definition: Combobox keyboard navigation and focus behavior depend on popup type; a dialog popup receives DOM focus.
patterns.guardrail: Do not apply listbox focus semantics to a dialog. Native select may suffice.
patterns.tests: Verify tab, arrows, Escape, selection, focus restoration and accessible state in a real browser.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: Static table versus interactive grid
patterns.definition: An interactive grid has a managed keyboard navigation model; ordinary tabular data may use a semantic table.
patterns.guardrail: Do not replace a static table with a grid role simply for visual styling. Editing controls can compete with arrow navigation.
patterns.tests: Validate row/column announcements, keyboard movement, edit mode and accessible fallback.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: Common region and visual hierarchy
patterns.definition: A perceptible container groups related elements and can outweigh proximity. Choose containment when it clarifies relationships.
patterns.guardrail: Do not surround all elements with cards or assume grouping guarantees task success.
patterns.tests: Compare a list and grouped variant with real search tasks and comprehension measures.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: View transition lifecycle and fallback
patterns.definition: View transitions expose lifecycle and skip functionality for visual changes. Application state and focus must be resolved independently of animation.
patterns.guardrail: Feature-detect, preserve an immediate fallback and avoid assuming support across all browsers or accessibility modes.
patterns.tests: Test unsupported API, interrupted transitions, reduced motion and route changes without animation.
patterns.classification: Source-backed synthesis; proposed acceptance test, not executed product validation

patterns.name: Error notebook from performance records
patterns.definition: The documented flow creates a separate notebook from incorrect answers in an existing notebook or statistics filtered by time, subject, board, folder and difficulty.
patterns.guardrail: Treat historical attempt events separately from current review status; do not infer mastery from a corrected retry.
patterns.tests: Create a fictional error set for a time range and verify exclusions, duplicate handling and source-attempt preservation.
patterns.classification: product-documentation

patterns.name: Retrieval practice and delayed retention
patterns.definition: The 2006 study compared memory testing and restudy with educationally relevant materials; later retention benefited from testing.
patterns.guardrail: Do not equate immediate fluency or short-term quiz accuracy with durable learning; generalization beyond the study tasks needs evidence.
patterns.tests: Compare delayed recall after equal-duration study and retrieval using equivalent original material.
patterns.classification: experimental-research

patterns.name: Spacing and retention interval
patterns.definition: The review examined spacing, lag and interstudy intervals in verbal recall and found the optimal interval depends on the intended retention interval.
patterns.guardrail: No universal fixed spacing schedule follows; the findings do not validate individual FSRS estimates.
patterns.tests: Predefine a retention horizon, compare schedules and report time, recall and uncertainty.
patterns.classification: meta-analysis

patterns.name: Question bank and reusable quizzes
patterns.definition: Items live in a separate question bank and may be reused in quizzes. Quiz configuration controls behavior; defaults include repeat attempts and post-completion feedback.
patterns.guardrail: Defaults are not mandatory policy; preserve the question version used in each attempt.
patterns.tests: Edit a fictional bank item after an attempt; confirm the historical response and grading remain reproducible.
patterns.classification: product-documentation

patterns.name: Graph link semantics and filters
patterns.definition: Nodes represent notes and edges internal links; documented graph filters include search, tags, attachments, existing files and orphans. Groups use color.
patterns.guardrail: Node size based on incoming links is not semantic importance. Keep explicit relation types distinct from layout.
patterns.tests: Verify toggles affect visibility without deleting underlying nodes and edges; provide keyboard alternative.
patterns.classification: product-documentation

patterns.name: Annotation database and PDF export
patterns.definition: Zotero stores annotation records in its database and supports exporting PDFs with embedded annotations, allowing individual annotation synchronization.
patterns.guardrail: Maintain export provenance and distinguish source document bytes from derived annotations. Do not assume identical conflict semantics in other readers.
patterns.tests: Round-trip an original annotated sample and compare annotation identity, target and text; test concurrent edits separately.
patterns.classification: product-documentation

patterns.name: Design token format interoperability
patterns.definition: The final community group report defines an exchange format for design tokens across tools, including typed values and references.
patterns.guardrail: This is not a W3C Recommendation or proof of accessibility; resolve references and verify actual rendered colors.
patterns.tests: Round-trip an original token group, detect cycles and undefined references, and compare resolved typed values.
patterns.classification: community-group-report

patterns.name: Point and interval selections in charts
patterns.definition: Selection parameters translate direct user interaction into data queries. Point selections target discrete values; interval selections target ranges.
patterns.guardrail: Selection state must be visible and clearable. Pointer-only brushing needs a keyboard-accessible alternative.
patterns.tests: Use fictional exam results, test selection and clearing, compare filtered row counts and accessible table.
patterns.classification: technical-documentation
patterns.demo_scope: Original ASCII text quote or fictional discrete selection; not full product conformance.

patterns.name: Concurrent search and stale response suppression
patterns.definition: An AbortController communicates cancellation to abortable operations. Pair cancellation with request identity to prevent obsolete responses updating current UI.
patterns.guardrail: Do not treat animation completion or cancellation alone as authority over state. Preserve previous results when useful; distinguish empty, failed and cancelled.
patterns.tests: Issue a slow request then a fast one; cancel pending request; fail and retry; assert current results and focus.
patterns.classification: technical-documentation

patterns.name: Manual tab activation and roving keyboard focus
patterns.definition: For manual activation, arrow navigation can move focus while the visible panel stays selected; activation changes the displayed panel.
patterns.guardrail: Do not confuse focus and selected state. Automatic activation is appropriate when panels can display without noticeable delay.
patterns.tests: Arrow to another tab; verify existing panel still active; Enter activates and changes aria-selected.
patterns.classification: implementation-guidance

patterns.name: Modal dialog focus containment and restoration
patterns.definition: Modal content takes focus, constrains tab navigation and closes on Escape. On closure, restore focus to the invoking control when it remains appropriate.
patterns.guardrail: Do not infer modal behavior from dimmed screenshot; consider invoker removal, workflow-specific focus and assistive technology.
patterns.tests: Open native modal via button; assert focus inside, Escape closes, and invoker receives focus.
patterns.classification: implementation-guidance

patterns.name: Item-bank lifecycle and immutable assessment version
patterns.definition: The Inep describes authoring, specialist review, possible pilots, and assembly against a skills matrix. A bank item and the published assessment containing it are distinct records.
patterns.guardrail: A public practice app is not the official item bank. Preserve item version, assessment edition, response and correction policy; do not import restricted items.
patterns.tests: Edit a fictional item's current version after a completed attempt; historical item, response and grade must remain reproducible.
patterns.classification: official-process-documentation

patterns.name: Item facility and discrimination statistics
patterns.definition: Moodle reports average item marks, attempt counts, discrimination and response frequencies. Low discrimination flags investigation, not proof of a broken question. First attempts and all attempts have different assumptions.
patterns.guardrail: Do not confuse item facility in a sampled cohort with a calibrated IRT difficulty parameter. Regrading must be traceable and cannot silently rewrite historical results.
patterns.tests: Use a fictional response matrix, label the population and denominator, test zero variance as N/A, compare first attempts with repeated attempts.
patterns.classification: versioned-product-documentation

patterns.name: QTI 2.2 and 3.0 interoperability boundaries
patterns.definition: QTI 3.0 was released in May 2022 and integrates accommodation features, improved web rendering and accessibility support, plus native support for adaptive testing and portable custom interactions.
patterns.guardrail: Exchange-format support is not proof of scoring equivalence, accessibility conformance or calibrated adaptive testing. Check exact version and profile.
patterns.tests: Round-trip an authored test item preserving identifier, response type and accommodation metadata; flag unsupported interactions instead of dropping them silently.
patterns.classification: official-standard-version-comparison

patterns.name: Educational and psychological testing standards reference
patterns.definition: The joint publication provides open-access English 2014 and earlier editions and Spanish access. Use it as a primary reference for assessment validity and measurement methodology.
patterns.guardrail: Publication availability alone is not chapter-level extraction or compliance. No claim of having read the full book. Separate score interpretation and use from practice-app interface requirements.
patterns.tests: For any high-stakes score interpretation, record the intended use and population, then obtain applicable evidence from the actual standard and validated assessment methodology.
patterns.classification: official-publication-index
